title: Salisbury steak with gravy, macaroni and cheese, frozen meal (1874)

content.title: About
content.content: This is a ready‑to‑heat frozen meal that includes a Salisbury‑style beef steak with a rich gravy and macaroni baked in a cheesy sauce. The portion is designed for a single serving and can be quickly reheated in a microwave or on the stovetop.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Salisbury steak dish originated in the United States in the early 20th century and is named after Dr. J. H. Salisbury, who promoted it as a nutritious, easily digestible meal.
Frozen versions often blend ground beef with beef trimmings to achieve a tender texture.
The cheese sauce for the macaroni is typically made from cheddar cheese, milk, and a small amount of flour for thickening.
Convenient frozen meals became popular after World War II when the rise of dual‑income families increased demand for quick, easy dishes.
Packaging from the 1874 era usually lists calorie content and ingredient breakdown according to the standards of that time.

items.title: Protein
items.content: The beef steak provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Calcium and Vitamin D
items.content: The cheese sauce supplies calcium for bone health, while vitamin D aids its absorption.

items.title: Energy Supply
items.content: A combination of protein and carbohydrates offers sustained satiety and a quick energy boost.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Beef is rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑Vitamins
items.content: The meal contains B12 and B6, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: High Sodium Content
items.content: Ready‑made frozen meals often contain a lot of salt, which may be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Saturated Fats
items.content: The beef and cheese sauce contribute saturated fats that can raise cholesterol levels if consumed frequently.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The product may contain milk, gluten (in the macaroni), and soy emulsifiers – common allergens.

items.title: Trans Fats
items.content: Some formulations may include partially hydrogenated oils that contain trans fats.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Defrost the package in the refrigerator or cook directly from frozen in the microwave. Heat on high for 3–4 minutes, then stir to ensure the gravy coats the steak and macaroni evenly. If needed, finish on the stovetop for 5–7 minutes until bubbling.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen meal at –18 °C or lower. Once opened, store in the refrigerator and consume within 2 days; reheat only once.
